title: Sequenced minor-version bridge with canary safety probes for private control plane
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement an automated, tenant-sequenced upgrade path for private (VPC) control planes that supports minor-version bridging and enforces runtime compatibility using pre-flight and in-flight safety probes. This ticket implements the orchestration and IaC changes (Terraform) plus the runtime health probes and rollback-indexing necessary for low-risk canary promotions across tenants.

Background: We frequently deploy minor control-plane updates that are backward-compatible at the API surface but require operator-level migration steps (CRD shims, webhook adjustments, schema migrations) and runtime warm-up to achieve latency SLOs. Current staged rollouts are manual and risky when multiple tenants with different traffic profiles are present.

Scope & Acceptance Criteria:
- Terraform modules: add a versioned upgrade plan resource and a sequencer that can accept a tenant cohort list and execute point-in-time promotion steps. Terraform changes must include state migration guidance so customers with local state move smoothly.
- Bridge strategy: introduce a lightweight "bridge" operator component that coordinates preflight checks (CRD compatibility, webhook validation, image availability) and runtime migration hooks.
- Canary safety probes: define preflight and in-flight probes (schema-check, KV-cache integrity, scheduler warm-up, token throughput regression) with pass/fail thresholds. Passing probes trigger the next cohort promotion.
- Rollback index: maintain per-tenant upgrade index allowing idempotent rollbacks to prior minor versions with automated data compatibility checks.
- Observability: new dashboard tile exposing canary probe metrics, percent of tenants promoted, and rollback incidents; automated alerts for probe failure and unexplained latency regressions.
- Automation: end-to-end automation from Terraform plan -> apply -> control-plane bridge orchestration -> canary promotion -> finalization. Manual hold/resume must be supported.

Non-goals: major version migrations (breaking API), tenant data migration tooling beyond small CRD/comms shims.

Technical approach:
1) Terraform: create a new module terraform/modules/controlplane_upgrade which exposes resources: upgrade_plan (list of cohorts), upgrade_step (preflight/apply/postflight), and plan_state (tenant indexes). Implement a remote state locking pattern to avoid concurrent promotions.
2) Bridge operator: a small controller (Go) with CRD UpgradePlan. It will call preflight probes by invoking existing healthcheck endpoints and perform temporary traffic mirroring when available. The operator will write its progress to a per-tenant annotation (upgrade-index).
3) Probes: implement probe harness in runtime that can run in dry-run and active mode; probes will publish metrics to the control-plane telemetry namespace (prometheus labels: upgrade_plan, tenant, step).
4) Rollback: use operator-recorded checkpoints + stored migration snapshots for quick revert. Rollback will run the inverse of postflight steps and validate via probes before resuming normal traffic.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for terraform module (plan generation + state transitions).
- Integration tests in private staging cluster with synthetic tenant traffic profiles (small/medium/high QPS).
- Canary drills: simulated probe failures to validate automatic abort and rollback.
- A/B validation against existing manual rollout process for two pilot customers.

Risks & Trade-offs:
- Complexity of additional operator logic increases upgrade path code surface and potential maintenance. Mitigation: keep bridge operator minimal and well-documented; prefer calling existing runtime endpoints rather than duplicating logic.
- Terraform remote-state locking could extend rollout time if a prior promotion stalls. Mitigation: implement timeouts and escalation hooks for manual override.
- Increased observability storage costs from probe metrics; mitigate by sampling and retention policies.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: Terraform module prototype + bridge operator skeleton (internal staging).
- Week 2: Implement probes, wire metric emission, and basic dashboard. Run internal Upgrade drills.
- Week 3: Pilot with 2 low-risk customers in dedicated staging VPCs; gather telemetry and iterate.
- Week 4: Open beta for select enterprise customers with opt-in coordination.

Acceptance tests (explicit):
- Create UpgradePlan via Terraform to promote 3 tenants in sequence and validate that after each cohort the operator advances only when all probes pass.
- Simulate probe failure on cohort 2 and confirm operator halts, runs rollback to cohort 1, and sends alerts.
- Run terraform destroy and validate plan_state cleanup and no orphaned annotations.

Artifacts and links:

- Terraform prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4218
- Bridge operator PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane-operator/pull/209
- Observability dashboard (internal): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/upgrade-ops/canary-safety
- Staging test results (log): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c-upgrade-drills

Notes: Coordinate with Product (PM-330) for pilot customer selection and with Security for the KMS/credentials handling in Terraform. The operator should be instrumented with fine-grained audit logs to satisfy compliance requirements for Private deployments.
